teaser: A FARA registration filed eight days after the killing, touching the same media network Kirk broadcast through — plus a reported TPUSA contact with a Hollywood synthetic-media firm. The file opens the section with "Can we confirm if this happened?"

title: Counter-UAS Gear Tested at Provo, Sept 4-10 (Claims)
description: An OSINT researcher reports anonymous claims that anti-drone gear was tested at Provo Airport in the week ending with Charlie Kirk's death. Uncorroborated by the author's own admission.
media_alt: This low-resolution, slightly blurry outdoor daytime image shows several armed individuals, some in tactical gear, dispersed across a grassy and dirt area adjacent to a dense wall…
teaser: Anti-drone equipment reportedly tested at Provo Airport during the exact week ending in Kirk's death, and DoD-badged contractors reportedly boarding an Egyptian Air Force jet there. The researcher states outright that he has corroborated none of it.

title: Drones Over the Venue and the Butler Comparison (Claims)
description: Researchers say they identified drones in phone footage from UVU and link them to the Butler attack on Trump. Compressed video is a notorious source of false drone sightings.
media_alt: This eye-level, medium-wide photograph captures political activist Charlie Kirk walking through an outdoor event venue under bright, direct sunlight.
teaser: Sixteen drones claimed in the UVU footage, and an anonymous NCTC contact who reportedly said the same drone-capable group was behind Butler. Compressed phone video is also the single most reliable generator of false drone sightings.

title: The Fort Huachuca JTF Meeting (Claims)
description: A whistleblower says he walked into a closed high-clearance meeting at Fort Huachuca the day before Charlie Kirk was killed. Attributed claims, not proven findings.
teaser: A whistleblower self-reported being at Fort Huachuca the day before; no source places him in any meeting. The document obtained afterward confirms he was there — not who else was.

title: Fort Huachuca Image Results Reportedly Wiped (Claims)
description: Stew Peters says Google image results for everyone his show named vanished the next day. With no archived before-state the claim is unfalsifiable, and an ordinary explanation fits exactly.
media_alt: This is a medium-wide shot of the exterior of a Brutalist concrete building complex during the daytime, focusing on a multi-level staircase and an outdoor plaza area.
teaser: A broadcaster says that the day after naming names, Google image results for every person named went blank while unnamed people still returned results. He kept screenshots of the after, and nobody archived the before.

title: Joe Kent's NCTC Foreign-Nexus Probe Halted (Claims)
description: Reporting says NCTC Director Joe Kent opened a foreign-interference inquiry into the Charlie Kirk killing and that it was shut down. Attributed claims, not proven findings.
teaser: The one intelligence component built by statute to answer whether a foreign hand was present reportedly opened that inquiry and was told to stop. The question was not answered and found empty — it was reportedly not asked.

title: N1098L: The HADES Aircraft's Low Passes (Claims)
description: Citizen trackers say an Army-linked ISR jet made two low slow passes near UVU on Sept 10, 2025. The altitude figures contradict each other inside the source. Attributed claims.
media_alt: This low-resolution, slightly blurry image shows a close-up crop of a man's face positioned on the right side of the frame, looking downward and slightly toward the camera.
teaser: An Army-linked ISR jet reportedly made two abnormally low, slow passes near the venue. The investigation file gives the same two maneuvers three incompatible ways, which means at least two tellings are wrong and none shows its work.

title: N560TW's Sept 10 Scottsdale-Provo Turnaround (Claims)
description: Candace Owens flagged a donor-linked Cessna Citation that landed at Provo the morning of Sept 10, 2025 and left again. The pattern is an ordinary light-jet day trip.
media_alt: This is a digital screenshot of a social media post on X (formerly Twitter) by user "George Webb - Investigative Journalist" (@RealGeorgeWebb1).
teaser: A donor-linked Citation landed at Provo at 10:06 AM on September 10 and turned straight around — land, sit, leave. Candace Owens is asking ground crews who was aboard, which is a request for tips, not a finding.

title: NSA Bumblehive Could Unmask the Foreign Phones (Claims)
description: Tony Seruga claims NSA's Utah Data Center could identify the foreign-registered phones he says were near Charlie Kirk at UVU. The underlying dataset has never been published.
media_alt: This is a two-panel vertical digital meme based on a classic unmasking scene from the cartoon *Scooby-Doo, Where Are You!*.
teaser: The accusation is not that NSA did something — it is that the capability to identify the foreign phones alleged near Kirk sits forty minutes from the venue, and the answer has never been produced. The underlying dataset has never been published.

title: Open Questions: US Intel
description: Twelve things citizen investigators flag as suspicious about US intelligence and defense-intelligence proximity to the Charlie Kirk case — Fort Huachuca, SAM-702, the HADES aircraft, the halted foreign-nexus probe. Attributed claims, not proven findings.
teaser: Eleven items about defense-intelligence proximity to the case: the flights, the installations, the surveillance capability, and the one federal foreign-nexus inquiry that was reportedly stopped. Ranked honestly, from the strongest item to the ones listed only so they can be retired.

title: Palantir Reportedly Linked to the Gun-Recovery Land (Claims)
description: An unsourced line in a working list claims Palantir owned the land where the rifle was recovered. The same list contradicts it, misspells the company, and cites no record.
media_alt: This is a digital news graphic produced by the BBC detailing the "distinctive" clothing of a shooting suspect.
teaser: The file's own words are "someone said," the company name is misspelled, and a second entry in the same list says the university owned the parcel instead. Published so it can be retired, not followed.

title: Provo Airport Badge Access List Modified 9/11/25 (Claims)
description: A one-line entry in the investigation file notes the Provo Airport badge access list was reportedly modified the day after the assassination. No document has been produced.
media_alt: This is a digital screenshot of a panoramic, wide-angle 360-degree street view image depicting a modern university campus courtyard, which has been modified with analytical…
teaser: One sentence in a working list: the badge access list at the airfield ten minutes from campus was reportedly modified the day after. No document, no custodian, no before-and-after — an observation someone wrote down to check, and nobody checked.

title: SAM-702 to Fort Huachuca — the VIP Flight Claim
description: Citizen trackers allege a USAF VIP jet sat at Fort Huachuca and left the day before Charlie Kirk was killed. No manifest has been released. Attributed claims, not proven findings.
media_alt: This eye-level, medium-wide interior photograph captures the third-row passenger seats of a modern vehicle, which are cluttered with stained paper bags and trash.
teaser: A USAF C-37A reportedly sat at the Army's intelligence home and left the morning of September 9. No manifest or visitor log has been released.

title: Hearings Closed, No Transcripts Released (Claims)
description: Citizen media report hearings closed to press with no transcripts issued. Attributed claims; closure is lawful and a news coalition is already litigating access — but the objection limits every other claim.
media_alt: This high-angle, close-up photograph displays a matte black, pocket-sized folding mechanical device—resembling a folded LifeCard single-shot pistol—resting on a weathered wooden…
teaser: Media barred, no transcripts issued, later sessions ordered closed as well. The page rates the claim EMERGING and says outright that closing a session is lawful and is not sealing a record forever.

title: The Death Notice Filed Six Days After the Shooting (Claims)
description: Commentators read a capital notice filed six days after the shooting as a rush to judgment. Attributed claims; early capital notice is standard and protects the defendant.
media_alt: This image is a clean, vertical digital screenshot of a formal text document denying a public records request.
teaser: The State noticed capital intent six days after the shooting, before the ballistics came back inconclusive. Read the ordinary explanation before the sinister one: in Utah an early death notice is what unlocks qualified capital counsel and funding for the defendant.

title: Defense Denied Access to Destructive Ballistics Testing (Claims)
description: A defense motion reports requests to photograph and attend testing of the autopsy bullet fragment were denied. Attributed claims; motion practice working as designed, not failing.
media_alt: This image is a clean, vertical digital screenshot of a formal text document denying a public records request.
teaser: The defense asked to photograph the bullet fragment and attend future testing, and was refused. The page separates the real January motion from the planted-evidence framing that got attached to it online.

title: The 600,000-Document Dump Against Continuance Opposition (Claims)
description: Posts say the State buried the defense in documents while opposing a continuance. Attributed claims; the two circulating figures differ by an order of magnitude and neither is sourced to a filing.
media_alt: This is a still image from a home security camera mounted on a covered front porch looking out at a sunny suburban street.
teaser: One post says 20,000 files, another says 600,000, and neither is sourced to a filing — a gap of more than an order of magnitude inside one investigation file. The timing objection survives the arithmetic; the numbers do not.

title: The Jailhouse Informant Transported Before a Closed Hearing (Claims)
description: Citizen media infer a jailhouse informant from a transport order they concede is their 'only logical explanation.' Attributed claims; transport orders are ministerial and issue by the dozen.
teaser: An inmate held in the same jail was moved around the preliminary hearing, and posters infer he is being positioned as a jailhouse informant. They concede it is the "only logical explanation" they could reach — not something any filing shows.

title: The Judges' Google Trends Claims (Claims)
description: A thread reads Google Trends as showing Israeli IP searches for two Utah judges before the assassination. Trends cannot report IP addresses, and the judicial timeline is public and mundane.
teaser: A thread claims Israeli IP addresses searched two Utah judges before the assassination. Google Trends publishes a normalized 0-to-100 interest index and does not expose IP addresses at all, so the tool cannot produce the output the claim describes.

title: Kennington Released With No Bail, Charges Dropped (Claims)
description: Posts read a same-day release and later dismissal as a cover-up. Attributed claims; every element has an ordinary reading under Utah open-carry and bail practice.
media_alt: This is a digital screenshot of a Google Trends analytics page displaying the search interest for the term "Russell Kim Kennington" over a 90-day period.
teaser: A man was reportedly arrested inside the active crime scene in a lab coat with a long gun, released same-day on zero bail, and had charges quietly dropped. Commentators cannot even agree on what the rifle in the photo is.

title: Open Questions: Trial and Legal
description: Twelve things citizen investigators flag as suspicious about how the Charlie Kirk case is being adjudicated — closed hearings, the publicity order, the extraction disclaimer, the death notice. Attributed claims, not proven findings.
teaser: Nine items about how the case is being adjudicated — closed hearings, a disclaimed extraction, a document dump, and an eyewitness the State never called. The section that limits every other claim, because a closed record cannot confirm or refute anything.

title: The Prosecution Disclaimed the Extraction Evidence (Claims)
description: A State filing reportedly says it will not offer forensic-extraction evidence — the source of the entire confession narrative. Attributed claims; most likely narrow lawyering, not a concession.
teaser: Prosecutors wrote that they did not intend to offer evidence from forensic extractions — and the entire public narrative of guilt is extraction-derived. Then an agent testified about a Cellebrite extraction in open court.

title: The Prosecution Never Called the Roof Eyewitness (Claims)
description: Investigators say the only person who filmed the roof figure was never called, and that DNA testing on recovered items stopped. Attributed claims; a prelim calls minimum witnesses by design.
teaser: The one person who says he saw and filmed the roof figure in full black tactical gear was reportedly never called, and told police they had the wrong man. DNA testing on items along the escape route was reportedly stopped.

title: Erika Kirk-Linked Lawyers Opposed the Continuance (Claims)
description: Commentators question why victim-side counsel opposed the defense's continuance. Attributed claims; opposing delay is the exercise of a statutory victims' right, not interference.
media_alt: This image is a digital screenshot of a post on the social media platform X (formerly Twitter) by the user Shaun King.
teaser: Lawyers described as Erika Kirk's opposed the defense's continuance while federal agencies had not produced files held since September. Utah gives a victim representative that right by statute — which is the answer, and also why the question keeps being asked.

title: Prosecutors Accused of Withholding the Rooftop Video (Claims)
description: A commentator back-calculates from a trimmed clip that the shot was impossible. Attributed claims; every input is an uncorroborated estimate and the defense has the full files.
media_alt: This is a digital screenshot of a news article headline on the CNN US website.
teaser: A commentator back-calculates from a compressed clip that the runner started two seconds before the hit, and calls the withheld footage criminal. Every input in that arithmetic is an estimate read off video nobody has in full.

title: The Acoustics Claim: Shot Came From the South (Claims)
description: An unnamed engineer reportedly concluded the shot came from the south. It is one of three mutually incompatible shot origins the investigation file asserts simultaneously.
media_alt: This is a satellite map image annotated with a timeline and route details tracing the movements of a suspect referred to as a "bomber" in Washington, D.C.
teaser: An unnamed engineer reportedly walks a 3D model to a shot origin south of the roof narrative. The whole entry is four lines with no name, no method and no error bars — and the file asserts two other origins simultaneously.

title: The All-Black Man the Construction Worker Met (Claims)
description: Electrician Dylan Hope reportedly described a man in all black right after the shooting. Early eyewitness and dispatch descriptions in mass-panic events are famously unreliable.
media_alt: Evidence image
teaser: An electrician says a man in all black told the crew someone had been shot. The page rates its own evidence and states plainly that panic-moment eyewitness descriptions are among the weakest evidence there is.

title: The Burnt Object in the SUV (Claims)
description: Project Constitution argues a charred mass in Kirk's SUV contains RØDE transmitter parts. The theory cannot resolve which RØDE model it is matching, and nothing has been tested.
media_alt: This is a low-resolution, close-up crop of a modern concrete building exterior, featuring a thick green circle drawn digitally over the center of the frame.
teaser: A charred mass photographed in the SUV is argued to contain transmitter parts, down to a melted audio jack. The theory cannot settle which RØDE model it is matching, and no fragment has ever been tested.

title: Butch Hibbs and Backstage Access (Claims)
description: An anonymous claim treats a pastor's brother having backstage access as suspicious. The innocent explanation is the one the file states and then discards. This page is a debunk.
media_alt: This is a digital composite graphic presenting information about an individual.
teaser: A pastor's brother arranging backstage access is treated as sinister, and the innocent explanation is the one the file states and then discards. Published as a debunk, with the unsupported family speculation left where it belongs.

title: The Canon XA55 Audio and a Third Boom (Claims)
description: An unsourced analysis claims a broadcast camera's uncompressed audio resolves three events including a detonation at the tent. Its own 120m rifle estimate corroborates the rooftop account.
media_alt: This is a still screenshot from a digital news broadcast, formatted for social media or a mobile video feed, featuring a close-up shot of a male spokesperson presenting at a…
teaser: Uncompressed four-channel broadcast audio is argued to separate three events: a Mach cone, a muzzle blast around 120 metres, and a louder low-frequency peak roughly 46 metres away — right at the tent where Charlie was seated.

title: The Claim a Group Blocked University Security (Claims)
description: A one-line unsourced claim that a group blocked university security, which the investigation file itself immediately questions in-line with the words 'Is that true'.
media_alt: This low-resolution digital image shows a group of people standing on a balcony or behind a railing of a modern building, viewed from a distance.
teaser: One numbered bullet, with the file's own author writing "Is that true" into the record as he wrote the claim down. No name, no footage, no date, and no description of what blocking would have meant.

title: KSL's Chopper 5 and the Screwdriver That Isn't There (Claims)
description: Citizen investigators put KSL's news helicopter N155TV over the Losee Center roof from about 1:38 pm on September 10, 2025, and argue its aerial footage shows no screwdriver where Officer Bagley reportedly found one. Attributed claims, not proven findings.
media_alt: FlightRadar24 playback showing helicopter N155TV in stacked orbits over the Utah Valley University campus at 7:38 PM UTC
teaser: A news helicopter is put over the Losee Center roof from about 1:38 pm, and citizen reviewers argue its footage shows no screwdriver where an officer reportedly found one. The argument turns entirely on timing and on what that camera could resolve.

title: The Mic Mounted Under the Shirt, Not Over (Claims)
description: The investigation file asks why Kirk's wireless mic was reportedly placed under his shirt with a furry windscreen attached. Under-shirt mounting is standard broadcast practice.
media_alt: This is a multi-pane visual analysis image consisting of a collage of four panels that investigate a specific architectural detail on a building.
teaser: The file asks in one line why the wireless mic sat under the shirt with a furry windscreen still attached. Under-shirt mounting is standard broadcast practice — and it is also the physical foundation the exploding-mic theory is built on.

title: Open Questions: UVU on 9/10
description: Thirteen things citizen investigators flag as suspicious about the venue, the setup, the equipment and the people at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025. Attributed claims, not proven findings.
teaser: Thirteen things citizen investigators flag about the venue, the setup, the equipment and the people physically on campus that day. The wider day, as distinct from the tight clock around the shot.

title: Tyler Robinson's Clothing Changes That Day (Claims)
description: Tyler Robinson reportedly changed clothes several times on September 10 and was arrested in his morning outfit. A limp appears and vanishes. He is charged, not convicted.
media_alt: This is a low-resolution, high-angle security camera image depicting a suburban residential street on a sunny day.
teaser: Maroon shirt and shorts at 8:29 am, black long-sleeve and jeans by 11:49, a pronounced limp at 11:50 that is gone by the 12:22 roof run. He is charged, not convicted, and the file itself lists these as questions.

title: The Executive Who Removed the Camera SD Card (Claims)
description: An unnamed executive reportedly removed a camera SD card after the shooting. Candace Owens has separately accused Terryl Farnsworth. The file does not establish they are the same person.
media_alt: This is a standard portrait or identification photograph of a young adult male, shown from the chest up against a plain blue background.
teaser: The file carries this claim twice and never reconciles the two versions: an unnamed executive in a bare numbered item, and a named allegation by Candace Owens. TPUSA has reportedly said police instructed the removal.

title: Six Campus Officers and No Ambulance Staged (Claims)
description: UVU reportedly assigned six campus officers and staged no ambulance for a 3,000-person outdoor event. Documented via a records request; negligence is the ordinary explanation.
media_alt: This high-angle outdoor photograph shows a group of heavily armed tactical law enforcement officers, some in SWAT gear, moving across a grassy slope next to a fenced-off road.
teaser: Six campus officers, no ambulance staged, no outside law enforcement coordinated, and faculty never trained on active-shooter protocol — for a crowd the chief later put at 3,000. UVU has acknowledged more documents exist and reportedly refused to release them.

title: Stairs Guy and the Backpack That Doesn't Fit (Claims)
description: Investigators argue the stairwell figure is a different person because the backpack and hat don't match and a Mauser 98 won't fit. The file's own backpack timeline contradicts itself.
media_alt: This is a composite digital screenshot of a social media post, likely from X (formerly Twitter).
teaser: A light blue half-empty backpack leaves the car; a dark, nearly full one appears in the stairwell. Investigators put the usable interior at seventeen inches against a rifle the file itself measures at forty-three or more.

title: The Body Flown Out, and No Burial Site (Claims)
description: Two one-line items ask why the body was flown out and why there is no burial site. The investigation file contains its own rebuttal: there was a public memorial, and a grave's location is family privacy.
media_alt: This high-speed action photograph captures the dramatic, mid-air explosion of a large, fluid-filled object, creating a massive burst of reddish-brown liquid.
teaser: Two one-line entries ask why the body was flown out and why there is no burial site. The file rebuts itself: there was a public memorial at State Farm Stadium, and a grave's location is family privacy. Privacy is not concealment.

title: Charred Material and Fragments in the SUV (Claims)
description: Photos of the transport SUV are read by some analysts as showing charred material and fragments. Nothing has been recovered, identified, or lab-tested. Reported claims only.
media_alt: This image is a forensic evidence photograph or document slide presenting physical evidence related to an investigation by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives…
teaser: A broadcast screenshot shows a pale fragment whose edges look scorched, and one question: why is there burned material in the SUV? Nothing has been recovered, identified or lab-tested. What is being analyzed is a photograph of a photograph.

title: Chest Wound Accounts Versus the Neck Wound (Claims)
description: Early witnesses described a chest or heart wound when the wound was in the neck. Eyewitness psychology explains this well — and the witnesses are private people who did nothing but talk to a reporter.
media_alt: This image is a digital screenshot of an anatomical illustration depicting a side-profile view of a human skull, cervical spine, and upper chest area.
teaser: The earliest witnesses on camera all described a wound to the heart. The charging document describes blood from the left side of the neck. Eyewitness memory of sudden violence is famously wrong about wound location — which points the opposite way from coordination.

title: The Empty ER and Hospital Personnel Changes (Claims)
description: Claims of a cleared ER and suspicious new hospital staff. The file contradicts itself three lines apart about a named CEO, and retracts one appointment claim inside the same section.
media_alt: This is a wide-angle, slightly elevated outdoor shot showing a massive crowd gathered on a university campus plaza on a bright, sunny day.
teaser: A rare page that turns on its own source: the investigation file contradicts itself three lines apart and retracts one of its own claims inside the same paragraph. Those failures are stated plainly instead of repeated.

title: The Necklace, Cavitation and Residue (Claims)
description: Two leading theories explain the snapped necklace — one requires a bullet, one requires no bullet. They directly refute each other, and one rests on a well-known physics error.
teaser: Two theories explain the snapped necklace, and they refute each other: one requires a fast projectile, the other requires no projectile at all. Presenting both as converging evidence is how a file talks itself into a conclusion.

title: No On-Site Ambulance and the Scoop-and-Run SUV (Claims)
description: Kirk was carried to the hospital by his own detail in an SUV, with no ambulance. An anonymous claim says a 911 call never reached the hospital. Hospitals do not receive 911 calls.
media_alt: This is a wide-angle outdoor photograph of a concrete courtyard and terraced amphitheater lawn on a university campus under a clear blue sky.
teaser: Kirk was carried into an SUV roughly thirty-one seconds after the shot — no ambulance, no sirens. An anonymous caller adds that "a 911 call never came through" at the hospital. Hospitals do not receive 911 calls at all.

title: The OR Timeline Versus the Jerusalem Post (Claims)
description: A reconstructed surgical timeline is said to end after the Jerusalem Post announced Kirk's death. Neither time is sourced, and the file elsewhere says he was DOA — which removes the OR window entirely.
teaser: A reconstructed surgical timeline is said to end after the Jerusalem Post had already announced the death. Neither time is sourced, linked or archived — and a foreknowledge argument is a claim about two clocks, with neither clock shown.

title: Open Questions: Hospital, Autopsy and Medical
description: Ten things citizen investigators flag as suspicious about the hospital, the transport, the medical examiner and the autopsy in the Charlie Kirk case. Attributed claims, not proven findings.
teaser: Ten things citizen investigators flag about the hospital, the transport, the medical examiner and the autopsy. Several of these items are contradicted by the investigation file's own text, and these pages say so rather than tidying it away.

title: The Timpanogos Surgeon Search-Trends Frenzy (Claims)
description: A post claims Israeli IPs searched seven Timpanogos doctors before the shooting. Google Trends cannot report IP addresses at all. Seven living physicians are implicated by a chart that cannot say this.
teaser: A recirculated thread says Israeli IPs searched seven Timpanogos doctors weeks before the shooting. Google Trends reports normalized regional interest on a 0-to-100 scale and cannot report an IP address at all. Seven living physicians are named by a chart that cannot say this.

title: Was a Nearer Level II Trauma Center Bypassed? (Claims)
description: A post argues Kirk was driven past a closer Level II trauma center to a Level IV hospital. The investigation file contradicts itself on the distances, and the conspiracy-friendly version is the unsourced one.
media_alt: This composite image compares a crowded outdoor event to a close-up detail of a modern concrete building facade.
teaser: Kirk was taken to a Level IV hospital when a Level II trauma centre was reportedly closer. The investigation file gives two flatly incompatible sets of distances, neither sourced to any mapping record — and the conspiracy-friendly version is the unsourced one.

title: The Wound Trajectory Entrance-Exit Dispute (Claims)
description: Online analysts dispute the official wound account — some say no exit, some say the neck IS the exit, some say no bullet. The theories cancel each other out. No pathologist endorses any of them.
media_alt: This image is a video frame showing the exterior entrance of a brutalist-style concrete building with large, dark-framed reflective glass windows.
teaser: No exit wound, the neck is the exit, or there was no bullet at all: three theories argued from the same footage, which is itself evidence the footage does not decide it. No pathologist has endorsed any of them.

title: Farnsworth Already Filming From the Rock Pile (Claims)
description: Terryl Farnsworth was reportedly filming from a rock pile 27 seconds after the shot and said 'He's dead' at 12:24:36. Critics call it foreknowledge; the ordinary reading is a bystander's reaction.
media_alt: This is a vertical screen capture of a video player interface from a social media platform, showing two young men in an outdoor setting.
teaser: Terryl Farnsworth was reportedly filming from a rock pile 27 seconds after the shot and said "He's dead" at 12:24:36. Critics call it foreknowledge; the ordinary reading is a bystander watching a man bleed.

title: Three Minutes to the First Police Report (Claims)
description: Police audio reportedly carries the first report of the shooting at 12:26 — after the SUV had already left. Two and a half minutes to a radio channel is fast, not slow.
media_alt: This image is a screenshot of a social media post on X (formerly Twitter) by user Matt Wallace, featuring a still from body camera footage.
teaser: Police audio reportedly carries the first report of the shooting at 12:26, after the SUV had already left with Kirk. Two and a half minutes to a radio channel is fast, not slow — which is why this one deflates on inspection.

title: McCoy Reportedly Phones His Wife as the Shot Lands (Claims)
description: A reconstruction places Mikey McCoy calling his wife at 12:23:30, the same second as the shot. No phone record or source supports the timestamp — it is an inference from footage.
media_alt: This image is a digital screenshot of an interactive web application designed as an "Investigation Dossier" or relationship-mapping tool.
teaser: A reconstruction places Mikey McCoy phoning his wife at 12:23:30, the same second as the shot. No phone record supports that timestamp; it is an inference drawn from footage.

title: McCoy Alone in Frame, Neff Nowhere (Claims)
description: Blake Neff has said he witnessed McCoy's calls, yet at 12:24:02 McCoy is reportedly alone in frame. This is a timeline-reconstruction question, not an accusation, and every premise is soft.
media_alt: This is a split-screen digital video still featuring a woman sitting in a podcast or broadcast studio on the left side, and a large graphic document titled "Mikey McCoy Call Logs"…
teaser: Blake Neff has said he witnessed McCoy's calls, yet at 12:24:02 McCoy is reportedly alone in frame. The investigation file's own author calls it a timeline question and makes no accusation — and nearly every premise, from the word "witnessed" to the clock offsets, is soft.

title: The N1098L Low Pass at 12:24 (Claims)
description: A HADES-program aircraft reportedly made a 335-foot low pass near UVU at 12:24, thirty seconds after the shot. An aircraft cannot react in thirty seconds, and the file's own numbers conflict.
media_alt: This is a digital screenshot of an iPhone text message conversation between two unidentified individuals, displaying incoming messages in gray speech bubbles against a light gray…
teaser: A HADES-program aircraft reportedly made a 335-foot low pass near UVU at 12:24, thirty seconds after the shot. No aircraft can react in thirty seconds, so the pass is either coincidence or pre-positioning — and the file's own numbers conflict.

title: Open Questions: Within Five Minutes
description: Everything citizen investigators flag as suspicious inside the ten minutes from 12:18:30 to 12:28:30 PM MT on September 10, 2025 — five minutes either side of the shot. Attributed claims, not proven findings.
media_alt: This is a digital screenshot of a Google Trends analytics interface displaying search data for the term "Russell Kim Kennington" within Israel over a five-year period.
teaser: Everything citizen investigators flag inside the ten minutes from 12:18:30 to 12:28:30 on September 10 — five minutes either side of the shot. Second by second is where the strongest and the flimsiest claims sit next to each other.

title: The Rifle Wrapped, Placed on the Roof, the Descent (Claims)
description: A compiled timeline says the rifle was set on the Losee roof at 12:24 — yet the Mauser was recovered in the woods. The tension resolves if the item was set down only to free both hands.
media_alt: This is a low-resolution, high-angle aerial or satellite 3D-rendered view of a modern building complex with angular roofs.
teaser: A compiled timeline says the rifle was set down on the Losee roof at 12:24 — yet the Mauser was recovered in the woods. The tension resolves if the item was put down only to free both hands for the drop.

title: The 12:22 Roof Run and the Vanishing Limp (Claims)
description: A compiled timeline says the roof figure limped all morning, then ran without a noticeable limp at 12:22. The entry carries no source and rests on an observer impression.
media_alt: This image is a digital screenshot of a post on the social media platform X (formerly Twitter) by user Kevin Sorbo (@ksorbs).
teaser: A compiled timeline says the roof figure limped all morning, then ran without a limp at 12:22. The entry carries no source and rests entirely on an observer's impression of gait in low-resolution video.

title: The Claim the Runner Started Before the Shot (Claims)
description: An unattributed passage back-extrapolates a rooftop runner's start to 12:23:28, two seconds before the shot. The arithmetic assumes constant velocity from a standing start, which is wrong.
media_alt: This image is a composite infographic consisting of five vertically arranged video stills on the left side, paired with black explanatory text on a white background on the right…
teaser: An unattributed passage back-extrapolates the rooftop runner's start to 12:23:28, two seconds before the shot. The arithmetic assumes constant velocity from a standing start, which is exactly where the two seconds come from.

title: The Shirt Pulled at the Instant of the Shot (Claims)
description: Exploding-mic proponents read a 4K close-up as showing an object driven up under Kirk's shirt. The theory's own cited explosives expert says the mechanism would move the mic the other way.
